title: Path pullbacks recognize cartesian squares in the coherent nerve of Kan complexes
statement:
Use spaces, coherent squares, cones and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the subset-poset coherent nerve of [def-coef-coherent-nerve-infrastructure]. Let $\mathsf{Kan}$ be the simplicial category of small Kan complexes with function simplicial sets, and let $\mathcal S=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(\mathsf{Kan})$. For Kan complexes $A,B,C,D$ and a strictly commuting square with top $f:A\to B$, left $g:A\to C$, right $r:B\to D$, bottom $s:C\to D$, put
$$P=B\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}C.$$
Let $q:A\to P$ have coordinates $f,g$ and the constant path at $rf=sg$. The strict square, regarded as a coherent square in $\mathcal S$, is cartesian in the limiting-cone sense if and only if $q$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. The assertion also holds for a specified homotopy-commuting square: a simplicial map $H:A\times\Delta^1\to D$ from $rf$ to $sg$ specifies $q$ by its path coordinate, and the coherent square must carry that commutation datum, including its triangle witnesses. Cartesian squares in $\mathcal S$ are invariant under equivalences of whole coherent square diagrams: an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(N([1]\times[1]),\mathcal S)$ preserves and reflects cartesianness. In particular, for any objectwise weak-equivalence zigzag of strict Kan-complex square diagrams, or any equivalence between a coherent square and such a strict presentation, cartesianness is equivalent to the strict presentation being homotopy cartesian. The path model and the comparison use the given commutation data; equality only of their four vertices or edge homotopy classes is not sufficient.
